utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. We were wondering whether we could start, with the consent of Defence counsel, only to deal briefly with a few housekeeping matters. I understand there are problems with the transport of the accused. If, however, you have any objection, we will not start. If you don't object, we could go through these housekeeping matters quickly and then wait for the accused, and only then shall we start the trial proceedings proper with the evidence given by testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My colleagues think that we could discuss the housekeeping matters now, and as regards the examination of the witnesses, we should wait for the arrival of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good. First of all, I see that the appearances are the same, so we will do without the appearances. Let me take this opportunity to welcome here our new legal officer, Dr. Michael Bohlander, who is a former judge from Germany, and I'm sure that from now onwards, we will benefit. By "we," I mean both parties and the registry and the Court will benefit from the competence and judicial experience of Dr. Bohlander. Second minor problem: Sitting hours. Except for today, we will have to sit from Tuesday to Friday from 9.00 to 1.00 because one of us is also -- actually, Judge May will be presiding over the Kordic case in the afternoon and he, of course, needs some rest and respite between the two trials. So we will, as I say, as from tomorrow, sit from 9.00 to 1.00 with one break from 10.45 to 11.15. Because we are talking of sitting, I should also tell you that Judge Mumba and I will be sitting in another case in two days which had been scheduled for Kupreskic, namely, the 28th and the 29th of June. After those two days, we have a Plenary Session of all Judges. That means that in June, we will be sitting from the 31st of May to the 4th of June and from the 21st to the 25th, but you don't need to stay on over the weekend because, as I say, we have to cancel the two hearings scheduled previously for the 28th and the 29th of June. Of course, we regret again having to shorten the number of hearings but, as I say, each of us is busy in other proceedings, trial proceedings, or appeal proceedings. Let me go on, unless there is any query. Otherwise, I will go on. Motions. Now, in accordance with a decision by the Bureau consisting, as you know, of the President, the Vice-President, and the Presiding Judges, so the three Trial Chambers, and in accordance also with a proposal by the Registrar, we have decided that from now onwards, we should all endeavour to have motions made orally and ruled upon orally. Why? This is mainly to save money, time, because it has appeared that the translation of so many motions in all the various trials is time-consuming and is also terribly expensive. So as long as we can therefore stick to the oral modality, this would be most welcome by the President and the Registrar. I wonder whether I could, therefore, make an appeal to both parties not to file motions in writing but only to make them orally. We could think of a sort of practice whereby we have oral motions on particular days except for urgent motions; then the other party could be invited to respond right away, or if the other party needs some time, we can give some time, one or two days, to the other party, then we hear the other party, and then we decide from the bench. This, as I say, will be translated in the various languages and will appear on the transcript, but this would be a wonderful way of saving time and money. Moving on to a particular motion filed by Counsel Pavkovic for defendant Santic, namely, the motion whereby the Court should call [redacted] as a Court witness. We have decided to refuse this motion. Of course, it is open to Counsel Pavkovic to call [redacted] as a Defence witness. Let me also tell you that I was told by the relevant officers of the registry that one of the three Court witnesses, the lady living in Amsterdam, the non-Dutch lady living in Amsterdam -- I don't know whether I can say in court her name because I don't know whether she is a protected witness -- cannot be found because, actually, she left Amsterdam three years ago, but the unit for the protection of victims and witnesses is looking for her, it is trying to trace her, and we have some hope that she can be found. As a consequence, she will not be heard today, possibly not even tomorrow. So today we can start with the other two Court witnesses. Now, the one lady to whom we have decided to assign a pseudonym, we will call her Witness CB, CB, and the other one, the judge, probably doesn't need any pseudonym. Yes. Good. I shall stop now. I wonder whether there are any queries or any suggestions on procedural matters to be discussed before the -- yes? Yes, Counsel Krajina? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Defence counsel of Vlatko Kupreskic, in its motion of the 19th of April this year, submitted a list of witnesses which we intend to call. I have to advise the Court that yesterday, on Sunday, we learned that Witness number 4 on our list, Radoslav Simovic, suddenly fell ill yesterday and was taken to hospital. We were told of this late last night by the clinic in Split, by the hospital in Split, and we informed the witness office that we have to cancel his appearance today. We would like to ask Your Honours to allow us to call this witness between the 25th of May and the 4th of June if this witness comes out of hospital by then. If he should stay in hospital, we would like the Court to allow us to call this witness's wife instead of the witness, and she would testify regarding the same circumstances, as to whether the 14th or 15th of April, 1993, the accused Vlatko Kupreskic was at their home in Baska Voda, and we would submit a summary of this witness statement on time. It was only late last night that we received the hospital report by fax, we have not had a chance to translate it, but it shows that Radoslav Simovic fell ill yesterday, on the 2nd of May, 1999, and that he was received in the ward of the Split hospital. He has acute bleeding in his stomach and he is receiving blood transfusions. If it is necessary, I would like to submit this. We regret this, but that's what happened. It has not been translated, but I have told you what it says. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comments from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Your motion is granted according to what you suggested. So he will not be coming this week; he will be called on the week starting on the 25th of May. If he has not recovered, his wife will be called at your request. However, before his wife comes, you should provide us and provide the Prosecutor with a written statement. Good. It is agreed. Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if now is the right moment to discuss this topic, but as regards the decision not to hear [redacted] as a Court witness, who can, however, be called as a Defence witness, it is due to the fact that he cannot be reached by the Defence counsel, and witnesses belonging to other ethnic communities who cannot be reached by the counsel have so far been called as Court witnesses, and this led Vladimir Santic's Defence counsel to suggest [redacted] as a witness bearing in mind your decision of the 24th of March this year that there can be no transfer of transcripts from one case to another. Because the witness [redacted] was heard in the Blaskic case, we hoped to be able to use this transcript for various reasons, but bearing in mind that he cannot be reached by the Defence counsel, this is what motivated us to propose that this witness be called because we consider him to be an important witness. As regards the other witness, I do not know whether he will be protected, so I will not mention the name, but I have to tell the Court that the Defence counsel contacted this witness in Amsterdam a month ago, and we have information about her address and we will advise the Court so that they can contact her. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comments from the Prosecution on [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, Counsel Pavkovic is making a comment on this particular point, but I will abstain from making a comment myself at the time being. Thank you. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The Court is grateful to Counsel Pavkovic for explaining now the precise reasons why, first of all, [redacted] is important and the precise reasons why it is impossible for the Defence to call him as a Defence witness. In light of that, we now revise our previous ruling and grant your motion. So we will call him as a court witness. (Trial Chamber confers) (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We can simply tell the accused that, of course, we have not dealt with any substantive matter in their absence. We asked Defence counsel whether they would allow us to start proceedings consisting of dealing only with procedural and technical matters, but we have been waiting for your arrival before we call any witness. We will now start with our first witness, Witness CB, in a closed session. To the best of my recollection, this particular witness will be examined in chief by more than one Defence counsel. I believe that Counsel Susak will start and then counsel -- yes, I see. (Closed session) 15 16 redacted pages 8848 – 8928 (closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 21 1.34 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of May, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
